warnings: Concept only: human review required for brief alignment, originality, typography and trademark clearance, factual claims, font rights, full accessibility and production feasibility.

kit.name: Cedar & Steam
kit.tagline: A good cup. A place to settle in.
kit.audience: Local adults aged 25–55, remote workers looking for a welcoming place to work, and weekend visitors looking for an easy stop for coffee and a pastry.
kit.positioning: An independent, small-town Midwest coffee shop that makes specialty coffee approachable and gives people room to stay. Cedar & Steam balances the ease of a neighborhood stop with the care of a specialty café.
kit.promise: Order a specialty coffee without decoding the menu, pick up a fresh pastry, or settle in with your work.
differentiators: Specialty coffee without the homework: use plain-language flavor descriptions and make the familiar drinks easy to find. The coffee offer comes from the brief; the menu approach is proposed.

A stop that can become a stay: make takeaway ordering easy while giving customers clear information about working from the shop. The workspace is part of the brief; specific amenities and policies need confirmation.

do: Describe drinks in familiar terms and explain specialty terms when they help someone choose.
Lead with practical details people need, such as hours, directions, and confirmed workspace information.
avoid: Avoid insider coffee jargon and exaggerated folksiness.
Avoid unverified claims about sourcing, sustainability, or how pastries are made.
voice.sample: Here for a quick coffee or settling in for a while? Start with the menu.

colors.rationale: A deep forest green for the wordmark, signs, and navigation. It anchors the palette without leaning on woodgrain or vintage effects.
A warm, light ground for menus, packaging layouts, and web pages.
Adds warmth to secondary panels and printed inserts without competing with the primary green.
A near-black for body copy, prices, hours, and other details that need to read quickly.
A distinct red-orange for pastry callouts, label tabs, and selective web accents. Pair it with text or an icon when it carries meaning.

typography.heading: Literata Semibold, in mixed case, for display headlines and menu section titles.
typography.body: Source Sans 3 Regular for descriptions and practical details; Semibold for labels and navigation.
typography.fallback: Georgia, serif for headings; system-ui, Arial, sans-serif for body.
typography.rationale: A crisp serif adds warmth without distressed farmhouse styling. The sans serif separates prices, hours, and navigation from expressive headlines. Test the full name in both one-line and stacked layouts, and keep mobile menu copy as live text.
typography.licensingCheck: Before adoption, verify the exact font files, availability, ampersand and currency glyphs, commercial print and web embedding rights, and any redistribution terms for vendor handoff.

logoDirections.name: Open Join
logoDirections.concept: Two offset, squared strokes interlock around an open center, like a timber joint left deliberately ajar. The compact, stepped silhouette suggests a threshold without drawing a literal door or coffee cup. Pair it with a mixed-case serif wordmark and an unembellished ampersand.
logoDirections.smallSize: Use a simplified symbol with a wider central gap for favicons and small stickers. Keep the full name on storefront signs and first-touch packaging.
logoDirections.oneColor: Use a solid Cedar Green mark on light stock or reverse it to a light silhouette on green. Keep the center open in both versions and proof the gap for ink spread.

logoDirections.name: Rising Ampersand
logoDirections.concept: Make the name itself the mark. Set Cedar and Steam in a two-line wordmark, with a custom ampersand beside the lines: a broad lower loop anchors it while a lifted upper stroke suggests rising warmth. The overall silhouette is a compact rectangle with one sweeping edge, distinct from the angular Open Join.
logoDirections.smallSize: Use the stand-alone ampersand only where the name is established nearby. Simplify its upper stroke and enlarge the loop opening for small digital and printed applications.
logoDirections.oneColor: Draw the ampersand and lettering in one solid ink. For the light-on-dark reverse, open up the loop and proof the thinner strokes so they do not disappear.

assumptions: The brief establishes the fictional shop's name, setting, audiences, offer, and positioning. No additional approved brand context was supplied.
Audience needs and the proposed menu and wayfinding approach are design hypotheses, not research findings.
Hours, seating layout, Wi-Fi, outlets, laptop policies, and pastry production details are unspecified. Do not publish them as facts until confirmed.
verification: Before real-world adoption, commission an appropriate trademark and local-market name review and check domains and social handles. Neither the name nor the proposed marks are cleared.

Verify the proposed text pairs in the implemented web design against WCAG 2.2 AA. Separately test controls, focus states, keyboard navigation, and mobile readability. Do not use color alone to indicate status or selection.

HEX values specify sRGB screen colors, not press targets. Check vendor profiles, stocks, finishes, minimum strokes and gaps, and physical proofs for each application. Verify applicable signage rules and packaging requirements.
nextSteps: Sketch both directions and compare them on a storefront sign, pastry bag, and mobile homepage before selecting one.
For signage, prioritize the full name in strong contrast. Test legibility from actual approach distances in daylight and after dark, and keep door hours separate so they are easy to update.

For packaging, prototype a one-ink pastry bag and use Ember Clay on an optional sticker for item identification. Reserve room for applicable product and allergen information, and proof ink spread and color on the chosen stock.
For web, put Menu, Hours, and Directions within easy reach on mobile. Use an HTML menu rather than an image-only menu, and publish workspace details only once confirmed.
